c: Microsoft Exchange (on-premises) and other servers in Windows domain environments often support Windows authentication using the NTLM and/or GSSAPI (Kerberos) SASL mechanisms. These allow an application

Many email providers, including Gmail and Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online), have disabled (or are in the process of disabling) password-based authentication for IMAP, POP3 and SMTP. Instead, applications

SmtpClient , Pop3Client and ImapClient all authenticate using SASL (Simple Authentication and Security Layer) mechanisms. This topic explains how MailKit chooses a mechanism and how to choose one yourself.

SmtpClient , Pop3Client and ImapClient all derive from MailService , so connecting, securing the connection, authenticating, logging and error handling work the same way regardless of which protocol you
